theory Cardinality

Cardinality

Equipollence, finite segments, and the pigeonhole principle.

Constable et al. §11.3

Cardinality, following Constable et al., *Implementing Mathematics with the Nuprl Proof Development System* (1986), §11.3.

The library there develops two layers:

1. Equipollence (bijections) as the definition of “same cardinality”, shown to be an equivalence relation (Figure 11.5). 2. The pigeonhole principle on finite integer segments {1..n} (Figure 11.4), whose extract finds a collision of a function from a larger finite set into a smaller one.

Finite cardinals are represented in two ways, both standard in CTT: integer segments `{s:Int | 0 &lt; s ∧ s &lt; n + 1}` (the book’s `{1..n}`), and the disjoint-union encoding `True ⊎ True` of a two-element type. The computational content of pigeonhole is proved on the latter, where case analysis is primitive; membership lemmas record the segment encoding.

15 theorems, 9 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any coloured phrase; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

examples/cardinality.nuprl

Original .nuprl file
-- | Cardinality, following Constable et al., *Implementing Mathematics with
-- the Nuprl Proof Development System* (1986), §11.3.
--
-- The library there develops two layers:
--
--   1. Equipollence (bijections) as the definition of “same cardinality”,
--      shown to be an equivalence relation (Figure 11.5).
--   2. The pigeonhole principle on finite integer segments {1..n}
--      (Figure 11.4), whose extract finds a collision of a function from a
--      larger finite set into a smaller one.
--
-- Finite cardinals are represented in two ways, both standard in CTT:
-- integer segments `{s:Int | 0 &lt; s ∧ s &lt; n + 1}` (the book’s `{1..n}`),
-- and the disjoint-union encoding `True ⊎ True` of a two-element type.
-- The computational content of pigeonhole is proved on the latter, where
-- case analysis is primitive; membership lemmas record the segment encoding.
theory Cardinality

comment book "Constable et al. §11.3: cardinality, equipollence, pigeonhole."

-- Positive integers and finite initial segments of the positives
-- (Figure 11.4: P and {1..m}).
abs Positive == {p:Int | 0 &lt; p}
abs Fin(n) == {s:Int | 0 &lt; s ∧ s &lt; n + 1}
abs Neq(x; y) == ¬(x = y ∈ Int)

-- Small finite types as disjoint unions (Bool ≅ 2, and 1 + 2 ≅ 3).
abs One == True
abs Two == True ⊎ True
abs Three == True ⊎ (True ⊎ True)

-- Equipollence: a constructive bijection (Figure 11.5).
abs Equipollent(A; B) ==
  ∃f:(A → B). ∃g:(B → A).
    (∀x:A. g (f x) = x ∈ A) ∧ (∀y:B. f (g y) = y ∈ B)

abs Injective(A; B; f) ==
  ∀x:A. ∀y:A. (f x = f y ∈ B) → x = y ∈ A

abs Surjective(A; B; f) ==
  ∀y:B. ∃x:A. f x = y ∈ B

soft Positive, Fin, Neq, One, Two, Three, Equipollent, Injective, Surjective

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Integer comparisons and finite segments
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Closed comparisons compute to Unit / Void, as in the integer rules.
theorem zero_lt_one :
  0 &lt; 1
proof
  intro
qed

theorem not_one_lt_zero :
  ¬(1 &lt; 0)
proof
  intro p
  elim 1
qed

-- lemma_arith of Figure 11.4: equality on Int is decidable.
theorem lemma_arith :
  ∀x:Int. ∀y:Int. x = y ∈ Int ∨ ¬(x = y ∈ Int)
proof
  intro x
  intro y
  decide x = y THENL [left THEN hyp, right THEN hyp]
qed

-- 1 inhabits the singleton segment {1..1} and the positives.
theorem one_in_fin1 :
  1 ∈ {s:Int | 0 &lt; s ∧ s &lt; 2}
proof
  auto
qed

theorem one_is_positive :
  1 ∈ {p:Int | 0 &lt; p}
proof
  auto
qed

theorem two_in_fin2 :
  2 ∈ {s:Int | 0 &lt; s ∧ s &lt; 3}
proof
  auto
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Equipollence is an equivalence relation (Figure 11.5)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem equipollent_refl :
  ∀A:U{i}. Equipollent(A; A)
proof
  intro A
  exists (λx. x) THENL [
    auto,
    exists (λx. x) THENL [
      auto,
      split THENL [intro x THEN auto, intro y THEN auto]
    ]
  ]
qed

theorem equipollent_sym :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. Equipollent(A; B) → Equipollent(B; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro p
  elim 3
  elim 5
  elim 7
  exists u1 THENL [hyp, exists u THENL [hyp, split THENL [hyp 9, hyp 8]]]
qed

theorem equipollent_trans :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀C:U{i}.
    Equipollent(A; B) → Equipollent(B; C) → Equipollent(A; C)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro C
  intro pAB
  intro pBC
  elim 4
  elim 7
  elim 9
  elim 5
  elim 13
  elim 15
  exists (λx. u3 (u x)) THENL [
    auto,
    exists (λz. u1 (u4 z)) THENL [
      auto,
      split THENL [
        intro x THEN elim 16 with (u x) THENL [
          auto,
          elim 19 THEN elim 10 with x THENL [hyp, hyp]
        ],
        intro z THEN elim 11 with (u4 z) THENL [
          auto,
          elim 19 THEN elim 17 with z THENL [hyp, hyp]
        ]
      ]
    ]
  ]
qed

-- A left inverse is enough for injectivity.
theorem left_inverse_injective :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀f:(A → B). ∀g:(B → A).
    (∀x:A. g (f x) = x ∈ A) →
    ∀x:A. ∀y:A. (f x = f y ∈ B) → x = y ∈ A
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro f
  intro g
  intro inv
  intro x
  intro y
  intro p
  elim 5 with x THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 9 THEN elim 5 with y THENL [
      hyp,
      elim 10 THEN elim 8 THEN auto
    ]
  ]
qed

theorem id_injective :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀x:A. ∀y:A. ((λz. z) x = (λz. z) y ∈ A) → x = y ∈ A
proof
  intro A
  intro x
  intro y
  intro p
  elim 4 THEN auto
qed

theorem id_surjective :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀y:A. ∃x:A. (λz. z) x = y ∈ A
proof
  intro A
  intro y
  exists y THENL [hyp, auto]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Pigeonhole principle (computational content of Figure 11.4)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The two injections into a two-element type are distinct.
theorem two_inl_inr_neq :
  ¬(inl Ax = inr Ax ∈ True ⊎ True)
proof
  intro p
  elim 1
qed

-- Any map from a 2-element type into a singleton collides. The extract is
-- the pair of distinct domain points (inl Ax, inr Ax); the range equality
-- is Unit-η.
theorem php_two_one :
  ∀f:(True ⊎ True) → True.
    ∃i:(True ⊎ True). ∃j:(True ⊎ True).
      ¬(i = j ∈ True ⊎ True) ∧ f i = f j ∈ True
proof
  intro f
  exists (inl Ax) THENL [
    auto,
    exists (inr Ax) THENL [
      auto,
      split THENL [intro p THEN elim 2, eq]
    ]
  ]
qed

-- lemma_1 of Figure 11.4 in the 3-into-2 case: any function from a
-- 3-element type into a 2-element type has a collision. The extract is a
-- pair of distinct domain points that f identifies. Cases follow the
-- book’s use of lemma_hole (search the image) by deciding f at each
-- canonical point.
theorem php_three_two :
  ∀f:(True ⊎ (True ⊎ True)) → (True ⊎ True).
    ∃i:(True ⊎ (True ⊎ True)). ∃j:(True ⊎ (True ⊎ True)).
      ¬(i = j ∈ True ⊎ (True ⊎ True)) ∧ f i = f j ∈ True ⊎ True
proof
  intro f
  decide (f (inl Ax)) THENL [
    auto,
    decide (f (inr (inl Ax))) THENL [
      auto,
      exists (inl Ax) THENL [
        auto,
        exists (inr (inl Ax)) THENL [
          auto,
          split THENL [
            intro p THEN elim 6,
            elim 3 THEN elim 5 THEN auto
          ]
        ]
      ],
      decide (f (inr (inr Ax))) THENL [
        auto,
        exists (inl Ax) THENL [
          auto,
          exists (inr (inr Ax)) THENL [
            auto,
            split THENL [
              intro p THEN elim 8,
              elim 3 THEN elim 7 THEN auto
            ]
          ]
        ],
        exists (inr (inl Ax)) THENL [
          auto,
          exists (inr (inr Ax)) THENL [
            auto,
            split THENL [
              intro p THEN elim 8,
              elim 5 THEN elim 7 THEN auto
            ]
          ]
        ]
      ]
    ],
    decide (f (inr (inl Ax))) THENL [
      auto,
      decide (f (inr (inr Ax))) THENL [
        auto,
        exists (inr (inl Ax)) THENL [
          auto,
          exists (inr (inr Ax)) THENL [
            auto,
            split THENL [
              intro p THEN elim 8,
              elim 5 THEN elim 7 THEN auto
            ]
          ]
        ],
        exists (inl Ax) THENL [
          auto,
          exists (inr (inr Ax)) THENL [
            auto,
            split THENL [
              intro p THEN elim 8,
              elim 3 THEN elim 7 THEN auto
            ]
          ]
        ]
      ],
      exists (inl Ax) THENL [
        auto,
        exists (inr (inl Ax)) THENL [
          auto,
          split THENL [
            intro p THEN elim 6,
            elim 3 THEN elim 5 THEN auto
          ]
        ]
      ]
    ]
  ]
qed
